column1: # prose-claims-allow.tsv — the exemption ratchet for `scripts/check-prose-claims.py`.
# FOUR TAB-separated fields:
#     path <TAB> rule <TAB> the claim text, escaped to one line <TAB> why it stays
# Keyed by the TEXT, not a line number: lanes move lines all day and a line-number key
# rots into a blanket ignore inside a day. ⚑ A row whose text no longer appears at that
# path FAILS the gate — repairing a doc RETIRES its exemption rather than leaving a
# permission slip behind. A reason under 20 characters FAILS: "ok" and "fine" are not
# reasons, and an exemption nobody had to justify is a mute with extra steps.
# ── TWO KINDS OF ROW, AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS ──────────────────────────────────
# EXEMPTION   the claim is FINE AS WRITTEN and the scanner is imprecise here. The reason
#             says why the sentence is true. There are currently ZERO of these, and that
#             is the state to keep the file in.
# HARVEST     the claim is FALSE and this gate found it. The reason begins `HARVEST
#             <date>:` and names the correction. It is baselined so the gate is green on
#             arrival and reds on the NEXT one — the same shape as
#             `scripts/mirror-gates/baseline.txt`, for the same reason: a gate whose
#             first run is a wall of true findings gets switched off before it has ever
#             caught anything.
#             ⚠ HARVEST rows are CAPPED. `HARVEST_CEILING` in the checker is a number in
#             reviewed code, currently 12; a thirteenth harvest row FAILS until a repair
#             lowers it. Baselining is therefore a one-way door: a row can be retired,
#             but not added without editing the ceiling in a visible diff.
# Twelve modules under `metatheory/Dregg2/` say in their own headers that the `Dregg2`
# root does not import them. It does. Eight are DIRECT `import` lines in
# `metatheory/Dregg2.lean`; four arrive transitively through a module the root imports.
# The sentence is load-bearing in this tree — it is how a reader decides whether a
# module's `#assert_axioms`/`#guard` KATs run in any CI target at all — so a stale one
# reads as "these checks are dark" about checks that are live, or invites a second
# rooting of a module already rooted.
# ⚑ These are NOT repaired here, on purpose. The Mina/FRI lane is live on several of the
# twelve (two touched within hours of this file being written) and a prose edit landing
# under a sibling's feet is how a shared tree loses work. They are recorded, dated and
# routed; each row names the one-line correction its owner should make.
